lead.headline: More Oil, Same Tariffs, No Ukraine: What the Shenzhen Summit Means at Home
lead.deck: Their first meeting touched fuel and farm trade, not Ukraine.
body: For the first time ever, the leaders of the United States, China and Russia met as a trio. Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for about an hour and a half on Thursday in Shenzhen, a Chinese city hosting the APEC summit.

Their short joint statement warned that “there can be no winners in a nuclear war,” and pledged more oil and gas. That pledge touches family budgets, because crude oil prices feed into what families pay for petrol, diesel, cooking gas and bus fares. Yet it gave no amounts and no timetable, and Hamad Hussain of Capital Economics called it “political noise.”

Brent crude, a world price for oil, fell to $90.33 a barrel on Friday, heading for a third straight weekly drop. Prices fell mainly because shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to about pre-war levels, raising expectations of a supply surplus.

Trade, the other cost families watch, stayed frozen. Tariffs are taxes on imported goods, and in the 2025 US-China trade war they climbed above 100%. No new tariff rates were announced. The truce agreed in Busan still ends on 10 January 2027, and Trump said he would ask China to “do some more” for American farmers.

One subject never made it into the statement: the war in Ukraine. Neither Ukraine nor any European government was in the room. Putin ruled out direct talks with Ukraine after a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch Bridge to Crimea. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky had called it a “huge mistake” for big powers to decide about smaller nations without them.

world.headline: A Night of Strikes on Ukraine Spills Over Into Poland
world.deck: Power, heat and water fail in Ukraine, and stray Russian weapons fall inside a NATO country.
body: While the leaders in Shenzhen left Ukraine out of their statement, Ukraine spent the following night under attack. Ukraine’s Air Force counted 404 attack drones and 84 cruise missiles sent by Russia, and Zelensky added 27 ballistic missiles to that tally. Most were stopped: Ukraine says 380 drones, 79 cruise missiles and 3 ballistic missiles were shot down or suppressed. Still, Ukraine’s prime minister reported at least nine deaths.

For ordinary people, the worst damage was to the things a home runs on. Electricity, heating and running water failed in places, and three of Kyiv’s bridges were hit. An energy official said one target was what they called Europe’s largest electrical substation. Zelensky said Russia sent its missiles in waves 20 to 30 minutes apart, which he said was meant to slow firefighters and repair crews.
Why this night? Three days earlier, on 17 November, Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge, and Putin promised a reply “far more painful.”

Some of the weapons did not stop at Ukraine’s border. In eastern Poland, a Kh-101 cruise missile fell near the village of Nowy Lipowiec, roughly 60 km inside the country, and a second missile and a jet-powered drone came down elsewhere. Nobody was hurt. But Poland belongs to the EU and to NATO, the Western military alliance, so Russian weapons on its soil raise fears the war could spread.

Poland’s leader, Donald Tusk, called the strikes a Russian “provocation” and met his security chiefs. NATO’s head, Mark Rutte, condemned “grave violations” of Polish airspace and was due in Warsaw on Saturday. Poland has seen this before: a Kh-101 also crashed there on 30 July.

india.headline: Cyclone Akvan Hits Odisha Weaker Than Feared After 3.72 Lakh Move to Safety
india.deck: The storm turned north and lost strength, but heavy rain and cancelled trains linger.
body: On India’s east coast, a storm from the Bay of Bengal came ashore on Friday morning. Cyclone Akvan crossed the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, with winds gusting up to 90 km per hour.

It arrived weaker, earlier and farther north than first forecast. The IMD had expected a very severe cyclonic storm to land in Andhra Pradesh around midday; instead Akvan changed course and weakened before landfall. Over land it faded into a deep depression, because a cyclone runs on warm, moist ocean air, and land cuts off that fuel.

Odisha did not wait to see. The state moved about 3.72 lakh people, or 372,000, to nearly 10,000 shelters, including 4,470 pregnant women; 1,450 have since given birth, and mothers and newborns are safe. Officials report no deaths or major damage so far.
Rain is the danger now, with red alerts in parts of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh and around 45 trains cancelled.
india.why: Odisha moved people before the storm’s path was certain. Families on the east coast still face rain and travel delays.

us.headline: Senators Say No, 48-51, to Bringing US Troops Home From the Iran War
us.deck: Three Republicans broke ranks, but the pullout failed; the next clash is over the war’s $48.3 billion bill.
body: Can Congress order US troops home from a war the president is fighting? The Senate tried on Thursday and fell short. By 48 votes to 51, senators rejected a measure telling the president to pull American forces out of the fighting with Iran, which began in late February. The House approved the same measure in September.

The result cut across party lines. Three Republicans, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul, backed the pullout, and Democrat John Fetterman opposed it. Even passing would have changed little in practice: this type of measure never goes to the president, so it could not become law.

For families, the bigger question may be the bill. By 13 November the war had cost at least $48.3 billion, and lawmakers face an 11 December deadline to fund the government or risk a shutdown. Some Democrats want to use that bill to cut off war money; others would wait until January, when their party controls Congress.

lead.headline: Three World Leaders Meet in China
body: The leaders of the US, China and Russia met together for the first time. They are Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. They met in Shenzhen, a city in China. The talks lasted about an hour and a half.

They agreed on a short statement. They said there can be no winners in a nuclear war. They also promised more oil and gas, but did not say how much. Oil prices kept falling anyway, mostly because ships carry oil through the Strait of Hormuz again.

They made no change to tariffs, which are taxes on goods from other countries. A deal that pauses some tariffs ends on 10 January. Ukraine was not at the meeting, and the statement did not mention the war there.

world.headline: Russia Attacks Ukraine, and Missiles Fall in Poland
body: Overnight, Russia fired many missiles and 404 drones at Ukraine. Ukraine shot most of them down. Still, at least nine people died. Three bridges in Kyiv were damaged. Some homes lost power, heat and water.

Two Russian missiles and a drone also fell in Poland, Ukraine’s neighbour. No one there was hurt. Poland is part of NATO, a group of countries that work together on defence. Poland’s leader called it a provocation, which means an act meant to stir up trouble.

india.headline: A Cyclone Hits Odisha, but People Were Ready
body: A cyclone is a huge spinning storm that forms over warm sea. Cyclone Akvan reached land near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning. Its winds gusted up to 90 km per hour.
The storm was weaker than expected. It also landed farther north. Storms like this lose power over land, because they need warm, wet sea air.
Before it came, Odisha moved about 3.72 lakh people to shelters. That is 372,000 people. Officials say no one has died so far. Heavy rain is still falling, and many trains were cancelled.

us.headline: Senate Says No to Ending the Iran War
body: On Thursday, the Senate voted on a plan to pull US forces out of the war with Iran.
The plan lost. 48 senators voted for it and 51 voted against it. Even if it had passed, it could not have become law.
The war has cost at least $48.3 billion so far. Lawmakers face an 11 December deadline to fund the government, and that could be the next fight.
